title: Selected shallow M7 to below 8 earthquakes had a larger nearby-event probability excess in both 2001-2012 and 2013-2024
abstract: We tested a binary measure of nearby earthquake activity in a fixed global USGS ComCat snapshot. We selected 272 centers with preferred magnitude from 7 to below 8 in 2001-2024. No other M7 or larger event could occur within 500 km and 30 days on either side. Neighbors had magnitude from 5.5 to below 7, lay within 200 km in three dimensions, and occurred on days 1 to below 7. We compared the probability of any neighbor after and before each center. We used common weights for two center magnitude bands. The shallow-minus-deeper probability contrast was 30.6 percentage points in 2001-2012 and 27.7 points in 2013-2024. Conditional 95% year-bootstrap intervals were 23.0-38.1 and 16.2-38.9 points. The contrast remained positive at 100 km, 300 km and a higher neighbor magnitude floor. The later-era contrast on days 7 to below 30 was unresolved. This gives a reproducible stability test of the known depth relation, not a new physical mechanism. Future-dependent selection, sparse deeper counts, broad magnitude bands, regional differences and catalog errors limit inference. Code, aggregate year blocks, an independent audit and source hashes are included. Source records stay outside the baseline package.

display.caption: After-minus-before probability and shallow-minus-deeper contrast for selected M7 to below 8 centers. Bars use common magnitude weights. Error bars are conditional 95% year-bootstrap intervals. Neighbors have M5.5 to below 7, distance at most 200 km, and gaps from 1 to below 7 days.
